entities.name: N-Phthalimide deprotection
observations: Reactant contains an N-phthalimide-protected side-chain amine; product reveals the corresponding primary amine.
Net transformation is deprotection by cleavage of the phthalimide group, not cyclization, condensation, substitution, or redox.
Closest empirical record uses hydrazine and water in ethanol at 85 °C for 3 hours, affording 96% yield.

entities.name: Hydrazine
observations: Specific supported reagent for this transformation; used with water in ethanol at 85 °C for 3 hours in the closest empirical record.
Hydrazinolysis cleaves N-phthalimide protecting groups and liberates the primary amine.

entities.name: Hydrazine ethanol deprotection conditions
observations: Hydrazine and water in ethanol, 85 °C, 3 hours; reported isolated yield 96%.

entities.name: Hydroxylamine
observations: Plausible alternative phthalimide-cleaving nucleophile; hydroxylamine hydrochloride with base is a practical variant, but it is not the directly matched record.

entities.name: Aqueous base
observations: Strong aqueous NaOH or KOH under heating is a possible alternative for phthalimide cleavage, subject to substrate stability; not the directly matched record.
